rubric: After emoji (or any non-ASCII text) are added to a function's docstring, code_index.py find no longer matches that docstring's English words: 'join path parts safely' stops ranking pkg/util.py helper_func first (score drops from about 21 to under 3 and other files outrank it).
trigger: Append 1,000 emoji to the helper_func docstring in project/pkg/util.py ("""Join path parts safely without escaping the root. 😀😀…"""), then run (cd project && python3 scripts/code_index.py find 'join path parts safely' --no-cache [--json]).
user_impact: Any docstring, comment or string that contains a single emoji, accented letter or CJK character silently drops out of word search, so find points users at unrelated files instead of the code they described.
intended_lookalikes: Emoji themselves are never index terms, so a query made only of emoji finds nothing; only CJK characters are indexed as bigrams.
The text form shortens a long source line to 110 characters ending in '...'.
Scores and the lower-ranked results (OAW's own scripts under project/scripts) differ slightly between runs on different trees; only the ranking of the described file matters.
find 'engine rotation' and makeEngine rank pkg/core.py through identifiers and the synonym list even though the words do not appear literally.
Files over 1 MB are skipped by design.
